basic_identification.name: Long-form generative art
basic_identification.originator: Coined/popularized by Tyler Hobbs (2021). Pioneered by Larva Labs (Autoglyphs, 2019). Platformized by Art Blocks (Erick Calderon/Snowfro, 2020) and fxhash (2021). Key practitioners: Tyler Hobbs (Fidenza), Dmitri Cherniak (Ringers), Matt DesLauriers (Meridian), Piter Pasma (Universal Rayhatcher), Zancan, William Mapan, Emily Xie.
basic_identification.geography: Global practice. Art Blocks (US-based). fxhash (France-based, Tezos ecosystem). Practitioners worldwide. Primary market concentration in US and Europe with significant Asian collector base.

core_ideas.core_claim: The algorithm is the artwork. Each mint produces a unique output from a deterministic generative script, with the artist relinquishing curation of individual outputs. Long-form generative art defines medium specificity for code-based art: the code is the primary creative artifact, not any single visual output. The on-chain script ensures permanence, verifiability, and independence from external infrastructure.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: The most digitally native art practice: the work exists as executable code that produces visual outputs through computation. The blockchain provides the unique seed (transaction hash) that generates each piece, making the act of collection part of the creation process. The medium is specifically code + blockchain + browser rendering -- none of these components exist in traditional art. The constraint of on-chain storage shapes the aesthetic (compact algorithms, elegant code).
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Complex relationship. The drop mechanic (limited editions released at a specific time) is inherently attention-driven, creating FOMO and speculation. However, the works themselves reward slow contemplation and technical appreciation. The shift from speculative collecting (2021-2022) toward aesthetic appreciation and institutional collection (2024-2025) suggests a movement away from pure attention dynamics.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Increasingly intention-native. The practice addresses declared needs for medium-specific digital art, permanence, and artistic authorship of code. The post-crash maturation has filtered out much of the speculative attention capture. fxhash's fx(params) innovation (collectors interact with the algorithm to shape output) deepens the intentional relationship between artist, code, and collector.

market_economics.revenue_model: Primary sale (artists set mint price, platforms take commission -- Art Blocks 10%, fxhash variable). Secondary market royalties (enforced to varying degrees). Art Blocks curated projects command higher prices. fxhash is more open/accessible. Art Blocks raised $6M (2021). fxhash raised $5M (2023) from 1kx, USV, Fabric Ventures. fxhash FXH token and art coins introduce new tokenomic models.
market_economics.market_position: Primary market (minting) and secondary market (trading). Art Blocks and fxhash are the primary platforms. Works also trade on OpenSea, Tezos marketplaces, and increasingly at traditional auction houses (Sotheby's, Christie's, Phillips).
market_economics.price_range: Enormous range. Art Blocks Curated blue-chip works (Fidenza, Ringers, Chromie Squiggle): $50K-$1M+. Mid-tier Art Blocks: $1K-$50K. fxhash works: $5-$5K typically, with breakout projects reaching higher. Open edition fxhash: often under $10.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Post-crash recovery with format evolution. The pure long-form format is no longer the dominant generative art release model. In 2024, artists and platforms are exploring other formats (editions, open-form via fxhash, interactive/parametric). Art Blocks reports 90% of projects now fully on-chain. Volume below 2021-2022 peaks but stabilizing at a sustainable level. Institutional collecting (Centre Pompidou, Whitney) provides price floor for top-tier works.
market_economics.collector_demographics: Initially crypto-native speculators. Evolving toward: informed collectors who understand code aesthetics, institutional collectors (museums acquiring for permanent collections), traditional contemporary art collectors crossing over. Post-crash demographic shift away from pure speculation toward aesthetic appreciation.
market_economics.sustainability: Moderate to strong for the practice itself; uncertain for platforms. The practice of generative art has deep roots (pre-blockchain) and will survive regardless of market conditions. Art Blocks and fxhash face platform sustainability questions at lower volumes. The institutional collection trajectory (museum acquisitions) provides a sustainability path outside speculative markets. Code-based art has intrinsic permanence (scripts on-chain).

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: JavaScript (p5.js, three.js, canvas), GLSL shaders, Solidity (for on-chain components). Art Blocks uses JavaScript libraries rendered in-browser. fxhash supports multiple languages including Processing, Python-based systems. fx(params) enables parametric input from collectors. Custom algorithms, noise functions, mathematical systems, L-systems, flow fields.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: Largely distinct from AI art. Long-form generative art is algorithmic (deterministic, authored code) rather than model-based (statistical, trained). Some artists are beginning to integrate ML components into generative scripts, but the community generally maintains a distinction between authored algorithms and AI-generated output. The code-as-art ethos emphasizes human authorship of the system, even when outputs are unpredictable.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Generative at mint, then static or animated artifact. Each piece is generated once (at minting) from a deterministic algorithm + hash seed. The output is fixed thereafter. Some projects include animation or interactivity. fxhash's open-form and fx(params) introduce more liveness.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Well-developed and still evolving. Key terms: long-form, generative, algorithmic, on-chain, hash-based, pseudorandom, deterministic, uncurated, flow fields, noise functions, parametric. Art-critical vocabulary borrowing from both computational art history (Vera Molnar, Manfred Mohr) and contemporary digital aesthetics. The vocabulary is adequate for practitioners but still forming in broader art criticism.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Openness (code often inspectable, some open-source). Commons-contributing (shared tools, open standards, p5.js ecosystem). Infrastructure over spectacle (code is the work, not the spectacle of viewing). Individual authorship within collective infrastructure (each artist writes their own algorithm, but platform and blockchain are shared).

infrastructure_governance.openness: Mixed. Art Blocks is a curated platform with curatorial gate. fxhash is open (anyone can publish). Source code of generated art is often inspectable on-chain or via the platform. p5.js and supporting libraries are open-source. Platform code is proprietary.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Art Blocks: curatorial committee (expert-committee for Curated, more open for Playground/Factory). fxhash: open publication, community curation, token governance emerging with FXH token. Neither is fully DAO-governed but fxhash is moving toward community governance.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Strong. Art is stored on-chain (Art Blocks: script on Ethereum, 90% fully on-chain by 2024). Artists retain authorship and royalty rights. Collectors own tokens with provenance on-chain. The art exists independently of the platform -- if Art Blocks or fxhash disappear, the scripts remain on-chain and can be rendered by anyone.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Good. ERC-721 standard tokens. Compatible with all Ethereum marketplaces. Art Blocks scripts use standard web technologies (JavaScript, HTML Canvas). fxhash operates on Tezos but has expanded to Ethereum. Cross-chain interoperability is emerging.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: Strong. On-chain script storage means the generative algorithm persists as long as the blockchain exists. Art Blocks has progressively moved to fully on-chain storage including dependencies. However, rendering requires a browser with JavaScript support. The longevity of each piece depends on continued browser API support. This is the most robust preservation model in digital art short of fully self-contained on-chain SVG.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Minimal in the platform sense. Artists consent to platform terms when publishing. Collectors consent by minting. No granular consent for secondary market behavior. Royalty enforcement is contested across the NFT ecosystem. fxhash's fx(params) introduces a form of collector consent/agency in the creation process.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Increasing integration. Art Blocks works acquired by Centre Pompidou, Whitney Museum. Regular presence at Sotheby's, Christie's, Phillips auctions. Inclusion in major museum exhibitions. However, the practice still exists primarily within the crypto-art ecosystem rather than the gallery system.
field_position.what_it_enables: Code-as-art at scale. Collectors participate in the creation process (the mint generates the unique output). Provenance and authenticity are on-chain. New economic models for artists (primary sales + royalties). Permanence through on-chain storage. A new aesthetic vocabulary specific to algorithmic art.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Critical infrastructure for contextualizing code aesthetics (criticism, education, institutional frameworks are nascent). Accessibility for non-technical audiences. Interoperability with non-blockchain art systems. Preservation standards beyond individual platform decisions. A unified secondary market with reliable royalty enforcement.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Artists without coding skills (though fxhash lowers barriers). Collectors without crypto wallets or blockchain literacy. Those who cannot afford gas fees. Non-English speakers (community discourse is heavily anglophone). Artists from regions with limited internet or restricted crypto access.
field_position.frontier_signal: Established practice, evolving format. Long-form generative art as defined by Tyler Hobbs is now established. The frontier has moved to: open-form (fxhash), parametric (fx(params)), interactive, multi-chain, and fully on-chain experiments. The practice is established; the formats continue to evolve.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Platform curation (Art Blocks Curated), social media (Twitter/X is dominant), word of mouth in crypto-art community, auction house previews, editorial coverage (Outland, Le Random, Right Click Save). Algorithmic recommendation on secondary marketplaces.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: Moderate. The practice depends on collector attention for primary sales. Twitter/X is critical for artist visibility and drop marketing. However, the on-chain works persist regardless of attention. Institutional collection provides attention-independent validation. If social media disappeared, the community would need to rebuild discovery mechanisms but the art itself would survive.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Increasingly intention-native. The post-crash maturation has filtered speculative attention-seekers. Remaining practitioners and collectors are largely motivated by genuine aesthetic and conceptual interest. The code-as-art ethos is inherently intention-driven: it serves medium specificity rather than engagement optimization.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Significant. Open-source tools (p5.js), shared aesthetic vocabulary, inspectable code that enables learning, community education efforts (Tyler Hobbs essays, fxhash articles). Art Blocks' move to fully on-chain storage contributes to permanent public infrastructure. The practice has established conventions and standards that benefit the broader field.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Ownership (on-chain token ownership chain). Creation provenance (mint transaction, hash seed, script authorship). Does not track meaning provenance (critical reception, exhibition history, cultural significance).
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Archival (permanent on-chain). The mint moment is singular and timestamped. The work itself is static after minting (deterministic from hash). No cyclical or anticipatory features. Some projects introduce temporal elements (animation, time-based variation).
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Does not explicitly address absence. The format foregrounds presence (what the algorithm produces) rather than absence (what it cannot). However, the deterministic nature means each hash-seed that is not minted represents an unrealized possibility space -- the algorithm's potential is always larger than its actualized outputs.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Coherence. The practice supports multiple aesthetic approaches, algorithmic strategies, and conceptual frameworks under the shared umbrella of code-as-art. There is no single authoritative style or approach. Tyler Hobbs' definition is influential but not prescriptive. Different platforms (Art Blocks, fxhash) represent different values (curation vs. openness).
coherence.contestability: Moderate. Art Blocks curatorial decisions can be contested through community feedback but ultimate authority rests with the curatorial board. fxhash's open model is inherently more contestable (anyone can publish). On-chain works cannot be modified after minting. The community actively debates what constitutes long-form generative art vs. other formats.
coherence.forkability: High at the practice level (anyone can write generative code and deploy on any blockchain). Moderate at the platform level (Art Blocks and fxhash have specific code bases that could be replicated but network effects are hard to fork). Code is inspectable and learnable.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The on-chain permanence model as a standard for digital art preservation. The code-as-art paradigm as a test case for medium specificity in A(DAI)'s taxonomy. The hash-based uniqueness model (deterministic but unique outputs) as a pattern for how structured systems can produce emergent variety. The community's practice of making code inspectable and learnable as a commons ethic.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The drop mechanic and FOMO-driven market dynamics. The platform dependency (Art Blocks as gatekeeper). The narrow focus on visual output that excludes other modalities. The ownership-only provenance model. The limited preservation strategy that depends on browser API continuity.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: Long-form generative art proves that digitally-native medium specificity is real and durable. It establishes that code can be the artwork and that blockchain can serve permanence. A(DAI) must grapple with how to classify and contextualize this practice without reducing it to its market dynamics. The tension is between the practice's genuine aesthetic innovation and its entanglement with speculative market mechanics -- A(DAI) must recognize both without collapsing them.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: NFT/crypto regulations apply to token sales. Royalty enforcement is a persistent challenge as marketplaces make royalties optional. No direct AI Act exposure (human-authored code, not AI-generated). Copyright law applies to the code and outputs. Tax treatment of NFT sales varies by jurisdiction. No specific regulatory framework for generative art.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Artist retains copyright on the generative algorithm. Each output is a unique edition owned by the token holder. License terms vary by artist and platform. Some artists release code under permissive licenses; others retain all rights. No standardized IP framework across the practice.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in. Artists choose to publish on platforms. Collectors choose to mint. No opt-out regime. Royalty enforcement is the contested area: some marketplaces allow buyers to opt out of paying royalties.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Depends on Ethereum (Art Blocks) or Tezos (fxhash) blockchains. Browser rendering (JavaScript engine). On-chain script storage reduces platform dependency -- if Art Blocks/fxhash disappear, the art persists. Secondary market depends on marketplace infrastructure (OpenSea, objkt.com, etc.).
ecosystem.network_effects: Strong. Art Blocks and fxhash benefit from concentrated collector communities. Shared tools (p5.js) create ecosystem effects. Artist reputations built on-platform transfer to off-platform value. The practice itself has positive network effects: more practitioners develop the aesthetic vocabulary and technical standards.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Pivoting and maturing. Volume down significantly from 2021-2022 peaks. Format diversifying beyond pure long-form (open-form, parametric, interactive). Institutional legitimacy growing (museum acquisitions, auction house sales). Community smaller but more dedicated. Price floor established for blue-chip works. The practice is healthy; the speculative overlay has receded.
